_note: English summary and tips for archetypes.json (AI translation of summary_th / tips, same faction order and index; name must match). Read by pipeline/build_data.py as summary_en / tips_en.

Monster.name: White Frost
Monster.summary: Put Frost on enemy rows, then drag targets into those rows with movement. Wild Hunt units benefit from Frost, and Dominance rewards you for having the highest unit. The sources describe it as an easy starter deck.
tips: Don't spend all your Frost in round 1. If you want to win round 1, pressure engine decks; otherwise save it for Caranthir to close the game.
Keep one movement card in case an enemy engine sits outside the Frosted row.
If the enemy has few units, don't put Frost on an empty row.
Frost scales poorly in short rounds; watch out for rounds that pass quickly.

Monster.name: Tatterwing / Deathwish Ruehin
Monster.summary: Decks seen often on ladder. Tatterwing uses Lara Dorren, while Deathwish Ruehin is built around Ruehin, Giant Toad and Brewess: Ritual; reviews say it has a higher-floor win condition than older Deathwish decks.
tips: Lara Dorren at low power lets you release Ard Gaeth, which works like extra provision.
Use Giant Toad and Brewess: Ritual as the Deathwish core, as in the Ruehin deck.
Koshchey with Kikimore Queen is a combo mentioned for use with Lilit's Omen.

Monster.name: Fruits of Ysgith
Monster.summary: An idea recommended by reviews: use Lilit's Omen to set up big threats like Mammuna and Gernichora in a single turn, for both points and tempo. Engine Fruits adds Alpha Werewolf and the regular Ciri.
tips: Combo Lilit's Omen with Koshchey + Kikimore Queen, or with two Deathwish cards for Overwhelming Hunger.
The reviewer warns that Kikimore Warrior is cheap and strong but only suits decks with good answers to engines.

Nilfgaard.name: Assimilate
Nilfgaard.summary: Create and copy your opponent's cards, so your options change every match. Good for players who like to improvise, and it teaches you other factions' cards. There is a starter version and an Enslave 6 version that is strong against engines.
tips: Play cheap Assimilate engines only when you have created cards to follow up with; don't expose two engines at once before the enemy uses their removal.
Win round 1 if the enemy has good targets to copy; otherwise save your engines for round 3.
If Double Cross offers three bad options, take immediate points or control.
Older starter decks may be over provision after balance changes; trim them but keep the Assimilate core.

Nilfgaard.name: Midrange Slave Infantry / Ivar
Nilfgaard.summary: The strongest deck around November 2025 according to reviews. It uses Slave Infantry and Ivar Evil-Eye to swap power with enemy units, backed by Sandor de Baccalà as a Deploy engine.
tips: Ivar Evil-Eye's power swap can reach a ceiling of over 30 points, according to reviews.
Slave Driver followed by a swarm of Slave Infantry is weak at high ladder ranks.
The sources say this deck has been nerfed; check the latest cards before using it.

Nilfgaard.name: Tactical Decision / Formation
Nilfgaard.summary: An armored soldier deck using Tactical Decision or Imperial Formation together with Affan Hillergrand, who is pulled from the deck on the last leader use and boosts armored soldiers. The Renfri Tactical Decision version is the most popular in NG.
tips: Affan Hillergrand fits both Tactical Decision and Formation, but you don't need to build the whole deck around him.
Vivienne de Tabris works well with Renfri's or Triss's Deploy.
Jan Calveit is the core of Shupe, which can answer engines.

Northern Realms.name: Shieldwall Engines
Northern Realms.summary: Shieldwall protects key units and supports cards that care about boosts, shields or surviving long enough to use their Order. It needs long rounds.
tips: The deck loses when it plays five engines but protects none of them. Open with expendable cards, then protect the important ones.
Contest round 1 with a small set of engines; don't commit Anna Strenger, Drummer and Immortals in a round you plan to give up.
If all your engines die, shorten the next round.

Northern Realms.name: Temple Zeal / Melitele
Northern Realms.summary: Temple of Melitele: Congregation is a high-ceiling, high-variance card. Reviews from mid-2025 call this the most successful NR deck on ladder. It creates three NR legendaries and returns units to your hand with a boost of about 9.
tips: Play Temple for carryover, not for immediate points.
Viraxas: Prince lets you reuse the Order of Prince Anseis or King Demavend, and works with Seltkirk.

Northern Realms.name: Spellweavers / Revenants
Northern Realms.summary: Spellweavers uses Cintrian Spellweaver as a scaling engine, copied with Chapter of Wizards or resurrected with Shani. Revenants uses Kaedweni Revenant with the carryover of Ronvid the Incessant.
tips: Spellweaver can be copied with Chapter of Wizards and created from Runeword; it works with or without Student.
Pair Revenant with Ronvid and damage cards.

Scoiatael.name: Nature's Gift Symbiosis
Scoiatael.summary: Each Nature special card can create a Wandering Treant. Hamadryad and Dryad turn Vitality and repeated Nature cards into a visible engine. An easy starter deck.
tips: Count board space, because Treants fill rows quickly; if it gets crowded, pass or play specials before engines.
Don't fire a Nature card just for a single Treant, and give Vitality to units that are likely to survive.
Aucwenn is the round-winning engine in non-Devotion Nature's Gift.

Scoiatael.name: Mahakam Dwarves / Elves
Scoiatael.summary: ST decks where, according to reviews, Mahakam Pass fits almost every version: Dwarves, Armor Dwarves and Elves, with the Elves version using The Heist. The information here is thinner than for other styles.
tips: Mahakam Pass fits almost every ST deck, according to reviews.
Gezras of Leyda is seen as a broken card in Dwarves or Gift decks.

Scoiatael.name: Harmony / Witchers
Scoiatael.summary: Reviews mention Harmony Quarixis, GN Harmony using Milaen as removal, and ST Witchers using Gezras. The information is thin, with no detailed play guide.
tips: Milaen is used as removal in GN Harmony decks.
Saskia: Commander was suggested for non-Nekker Movement.

Skellige.name: Patricidal Fury Warriors
Skellige.summary: The leader creates damaged units, enabling Bloodthirst and giving Sove a guaranteed target. Longship and Warrior reward damage that hits breakpoints, and Seagull guarantees carryover.
tips: The deck needs to control round length, because Sove and targeted removal are punished by short rounds.
Spend leader charges only on Sove, Bloodthirst or big tempo swings.
If the enemy denies Bloodthirst, stop holding conditional answers and just take points.

Skellige.name: Pirates / Onslaught
Skellige.summary: Pirate and Onslaught decks using Deranged Corsair in both PF Abordage and Onslaught Pirates. The Armor Exploit version uses Heymaey Protector for endless armor, but the cost increase of Tainted Ale makes it less attractive.
tips: Deranged Corsair helps both Abordage and Onslaught Pirates, according to the October review.
Heymaey Protector creates endless armor.

Skellige.name: Battle Trance Selfwound / Raid
Skellige.summary: Selfwound uses Svalblod and Portal and is very binary: it struggles if the deck has no answer to Sigvald or Knut. All-in Raid uses Highland Warlord to add damage to Raid, together with Blood Eagle and Primal Savagery.
tips: Selfwound is very swingy; without an answer to Sigvald or Knut it is in trouble.
Blood Eagle tutors Bloodthirst Warrior and has a removal combo.

Syndicate.name: Off the Books Sesames
Syndicate.summary: Shady Vendor creates copies of Open, Sesame! or Pulling the Strings, adding red-coin carryover. A style reviews saw often throughout 2025.
tips: Oxenfurt Guard plays for about 13 points for 4 provision in the mid-year version.
Shady Vendor adds copies of Open, Sesame! for more red-coin carryover.

Syndicate.name: Congregate Firesworn
Syndicate.summary: Create tokens, generate coins, spend coins, then turn the swarm into points. The sources call it the hardest for beginners. Firesworn Scribe gains coins when units are spawned; the Printing Press combo is Grand Inquisitor Helveed + Lonely Champion.
tips: Remember the core loop: gain coins, spend coins, turn them into points.
If your coin bank is full, spend before generating more, and stop creating tokens when the board is full.
Open with Scribe only when you have a safe coin spender in hand.

Syndicate.name: Lined Pockets Crimes
Syndicate.summary: Lined Pockets Crimes decks; the version reviews like uses Cleaver and Halfling Safecracker, with Novigradian Justice tutoring Safecracker, and Cleaver's Muscle at 7 power makes spending coins much more efficient.
tips: Novigradian Justice tutors Safecracker.
Ewald Borsodi can be used as a round 1 coin spender.
